newsitem.title: USA: USAir sees higher Q4 unit, fuel costs.
newsitem.headline: USAir sees higher Q4 unit, fuel costs.

text.p: USAir Group Inc said Tuesday it expects fourth quarter fuel and unit costs to increase over last year.
USAir chief financial officer John Harper told analysts that he expects the carriers' fourth quarter fuel costs to range between $0.70 to $0.72 a gallon, about 25 to 30 percent higher than last year.
As of September 30, USAir's fuel costs were $0.6128 a gallon, about 16.7 percent higher than last year.
USAir and other U.S. airlines have struggled with higher fuel costs, which have increased about 40 percent since June.
The Arlington, Va.-based airline also expects fourth quarter unit costs to increase two to three percent over last year.
USAir and its labor groups are currently in talks to reduce operating costs, which remain among the highest in the industry.
USAir's costs were $0.1266 per available seat mile as of September 30.
The carrier also said it expects to have a cash balance of more than $1.3 billion at the end of 1996.
